text:
On 28 October, ASCI published its review of nutraceutical ads in India. 60 of the 61 ads it reviewed broke the advertising code, across 32 brands.

One finding matters to everyone who buys supplements. Brands often take a study on a single ingredient and use it to sell the whole product.

We think the fix is simple to say and harder to do: let people check the claim for themselves.

That is how SILT is built. Every dose is printed on the pack, so you can hold it up against the studies. There are no proprietary blends. Each of our 19 ingredients has a lab report you can read, next to the research behind its dose. And we talk about what the studies found at that dose, never about curing anything.

It is slower and it costs more. In a category where almost every reviewed ad failed the code, being checkable is the point.

What would make you trust a new supplement brand's claims?
